head: claude/mi98-automation-landing-and-drafts
title: MI-98: automation PRs declare their own landing, and drafts stop being the hold
body:
## MI-98 — the automation PR lane, and drafts as a hold

Two halves, both from operator rulings on 2026-09-03, folded into one PR because they are the same pipeline one step apart (manager's scope call: a third concurrent `.github/` PR would be the conflict cost we already paid twice this morning).

---

## (a) The automation lockout

MI-88's landing route shipped this morning and met the machine-authored PR population for the first time. **Population measured at 09:10Z: 7 open automation PRs red-locked** on `R11 no landing declaration` — 3 `reconcile-open-prs`, 3 `work-digest`, 1 `strategy-reviews` — stacking up because each family re-fires on its cadence while nothing can land. `reconcile-open-prs` keeps `docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json` honest, so **the register that tracks PR staleness was itself the thing that could not land.**

**The fix is at the one shared lever.** Every automation workflow routes through `.github/actions/commit-to-main`, which now writes its own `.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json` **and** `.github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt` as part of the commit it already makes.

**Deliberately NOT an `automation/**` exemption in the guard.** That was the cheap route and it would have created an unguarded lane on the guard's first day — the "cheaper to lie to than to satisfy" failure this repo already paid for with `new-table-wiring-guard`'s presence-only marker. These PRs now make the same declaration every other PR makes and are graded by the same rules.

### Proven against a real locked branch, not asserted

`automation/reconcile-open-prs-33730997737-1`, before and after:

```
BEFORE: ::error::pr-landing-guard FAILED (state=undeclared)
          R11 no landing declaration at .github/pr-landing/automation-reconcile-open-prs-33730997737-1.json
AFTER:  pr-landing: OK — state=declared_self_land
```

### Two things I got wrong first and fixed by measurement

- **I wrote only the declaration at first.** The guard moved the failure from R11 to **R6** — *"a readiness declaration lands nothing on its own — that is precisely how 7 green PRs sat unmerged"*. Hence the arming file too. R6 was right and I was wrong.
- ⚠️ **`landing: "self"` is the TRUE statement here, not the convenient one.** `commit-to-main` arms auto-merge *itself* at line 196 with `gh pr merge --auto --squash`. Declaring `hold` would be a lie its own next step contradicts.

⚠️ The arming file is **inert as a trigger** on these branches — `claude-pr-automerge.yml` fires on `branches: ["claude/**"]` and these are `automation/**`. It is the declared-intent record R6 checks, and the intent is true. Written inert on purpose; do not "fix" it by widening that workflow's branch filter.

---

## (b) Drafts stop being a hold mechanism

Operator, verbatim: *"Going into github to marke drafts ready is not something we can include in the workflow"*.

A draft is **a hold its own author cannot lift** — sub-sessions 403 on `update_pull_request` — so every draft became a manual click for someone else. **Measured: 4 of 15 open PRs were drafts** awaiting a hand-clear, and the day manager hand-un-drafted three (including this session's own #10918).

- `pr-opener.yml`'s `draft` default flips `true` → `false`. jq behaviour verified across all three inputs: `{"draft":true}` → true, `{"draft":false}` → false, `{}` → false.
- `session_registry.py`'s spawn template: *"Tier-2 / Tier-3 — STAY A DRAFT"* becomes **open ready, hold via the landing declaration**.

### ⚠️ I verified the declaration is load-bearing BEFORE relying on it

Because if it were not, removing the draft flag would be actively dangerous — which is exactly the check the manager asked for.

1. **Nothing arms a PR that has not armed itself.** `claude-pr-automerge.yml` triggers only on `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt`; its own header says the file's *contents are never read, its PATH is the signal*. A `hold` PR writes no such file.
2. **An armed PR declaring `hold` is FAILED by R10**, a required check, and auto-merge merges only on green. Self-tested (`"R10 armed while declaring hold"`).

⚠️ **The honest trade:** the draft flag *did* buy one thing — GitHub disables the merge button on drafts, guarding against a premature **human** click. That guard is gone. Smaller than the auto-merge risk, and it is the trade the operator accepted.

`automerge-trigger-guard`'s **C5 is untouched** — the relay still may not un-draft a PR it did not open. The fix is that sessions stop creating the state.

---

## Two findings filed, not fixed

- **`BL-20260903-CHECK-PR-LANDING-ARMED-TEST-MISSES-THE-GH-PR-MERGE-AUTO-ROUTE`** — the guard decides `armed` by the request file alone, but there are **2 arming routes and it can see 1**. So R10 *cannot* fire on a PR armed the way `commit-to-main` arms them. Not exploited (the declaration is truthful), but it means the safe declaration rests on author good faith rather than a check.
- **`BL-20260903-TWO-AUTOMATION-FAMILIES-WRITE-PATHS-OUTSIDE-THE-TIER-1-SURFACE-AND-WILL-RELOCK`** — measured across **all 35** automation branches by family: the 3 locked families touch **zero** non-Tier-1 paths and pass R5; `ciwatch` (`automation/board-results/**`, 8 branches) and `research-queue-stamp` (`research/queue/*.yaml`, 2) would fail **R5** on their next run. **I did not widen `TIER1_SURFACE`** — that widens what self-lands with no human read, and it is a decision, not a side effect.

**So this PR unlocks 7 of the 7 currently-locked PRs, and leaves 2 families to re-lock later by a named mechanism rather than a silent one.**

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **62 PASS / 0 FAIL / 21 SKIP**, *"All relevant guards passed."* (21 skipped as not relevant to this diff; the full-suite number differs from a broader diff's for that reason.)
- The declaration writer was **executed**, not eyeballed: extracted from the YAML and run against a simulated `work-digest` environment, producing exactly `automation-work-digest-33730997742-1.json` — the slug PR #10914's CI error names.
- ⚠️ `manager-scope-guard` does not appear in this run because MI-95 (#10918) has not merged yet; this branch was cut from a `main` without it.

## Landing

`"landing": "hold"`, `changes_landing_machinery` — and **the condition is genuinely met this time**: the diff modifies `.github/workflows/pr-opener.yml` and `scripts/ops/session_registry.py`, both named on `LANDING_MACHINERY`. Concretely, a mistake here would open every future session PR ready when it meant to hold one. One human read.
